title: SQL Set 02: E-Commerce Orders, Anti-Joins & Filtering
description: Multi-table joins, HAVING thresholds, anti-joins with NULL safety, and revenue ranking across an e-commerce order schema.

queries.title: High-Value Repeat Customers
queries.prompt: Find `cust_name` and `total_spent` for customers who placed at least 2 `COMPLETED` orders totaling strictly more than 5000. Order by `total_spent` descending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE customers (cust_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cust_name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cust_id INT, amount INT, status TEXT);
queries.seedSql: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Siddharth'),(2,'Lavanya'),(3,'Pranav'),(4,'Zoya'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (10,1,3200,'COMPLETED'),(11,1,2400,'COMPLETED'),(12,2,6000,'COMPLETED'),(13,3,2900,'COMPLETED'),(14,3,2500,'CANCELLED'),(15,4,3000,'COMPLETED'),(16,4,2100,'COMPLETED');
queries.solutionSql: SELECT c.cust_name, SUM(o.amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.cust_id = o.cust_id WHERE o.status = 'COMPLETED' GROUP BY c.cust_id, c.cust_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 AND SUM(o.amount) > 5000 ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
queries.explanation: Filter `status = 'COMPLETED'` in `WHERE` before grouping so cancelled orders never count toward the 2-order minimum.

queries.title: Unsold Products in Catalog
queries.prompt: List `prod_id` and `prod_name` of all catalog products that have never appeared in `order_items`, sorted by `prod_id` ascending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE products (prod_id INT PRIMARY KEY, prod_name TEXT); CREATE TABLE order_items (item_id INT PRIMARY KEY, prod_id INT, qty INT);
queries.seedSql: INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Keyboard'),(2,'Monitor'),(3,'Dock'),(4,'Webcam'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (100,1,2),(101,3,1),(102,NULL,4);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT p.prod_id, p.prod_name FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.prod_id = p.prod_id) ORDER BY p.prod_id;
queries.explanation: Notice row `(102, NULL, 4)` in `order_items`: `NOT IN (SELECT prod_id FROM order_items)` would return zero rows due to SQL 3-valued NULL logic, whereas `NOT EXISTS` handles NULLs safely.

queries.title: Top Product Category by Revenue per Region
queries.prompt: Compute total revenue per `(region, category)` and return the top-earning category (including ties) for each `region`, ordered by `region` ascending and `category` ascending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE sales (sale_id INT PRIMARY KEY, region TEXT, category TEXT, revenue INT);
queries.solutionSql: WITH agg AS (SELECT region, category, SUM(revenue) AS total_rev FROM sales GROUP BY region, category), ranked AS (SELECT region, category, total_rev, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY total_rev DESC) AS rnk FROM agg) SELECT region, category, total_rev FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 1 ORDER BY region, category;
queries.explanation: `DENSE_RANK()` partitioned by `region` preserves ties (Audio and Tablets both tie at 600 in South).

queries.title: Order Fulfillment & Cancellation Rate by Seller
queries.prompt: For every seller in `shipments`, return `seller_id`, `delivered_cnt`, and `cancelled_cnt`, ordered by `seller_id` ascending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE shipments (ship_id INT PRIMARY KEY, seller_id INT, state TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT seller_id, SUM(CASE WHEN state = 'DELIVERED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_cnt, SUM(CASE WHEN state = 'CANCELLED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_cnt FROM shipments GROUP BY seller_id ORDER BY seller_id;
queries.explanation: Conditional `SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)` pivots row statuses into columns in a single scan.

queries.title: Above-Average Order Invoices
queries.prompt: Return `invoice_id` and `grand_total` for invoices whose `grand_total` exceeds the overall average invoice total across the entire `invoices` table, ordered by `grand_total` descending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE invoices (invoice_id INT PRIMARY KEY, grand_total INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT invoice_id, grand_total FROM invoices WHERE grand_total > (SELECT AVG(grand_total) FROM invoices) ORDER BY grand_total DESC;
queries.explanation: Overall average is `(100+200+300+600)/4 = 300`; only invoice 4 (600) is strictly greater than 300.
